title: Add multi-customer participants to Container Loading List
description: Close the audited multi-customer consolidation gap by adding an authoritative, bounded participant list beneath an existing Container Loading List. Preserve the legacy single CustomerId as the compatibility primary-customer field and do not backfill historical containers during normal reads. This task may add repository schema code and validate against non-production test databases, but it must not allocate expenses, rewrite loading details, mutate Trade Documents, execute production SQL, deploy, or release.
acceptance_criteria: Users can maintain one or more distinct Customer participants for a Container Loading List and explicitly designate exactly one active participant as primary.
Each new participant references an existing active Customer; duplicate active Customer entries in the same loading list are rejected, and deleted or inactive Customers cannot be newly selected.
Participant records preserve bounded Customer code and name snapshots so a later unavailable Customer remains readable and is clearly marked unavailable rather than silently replaced.

For a loading list with participant rows, the explicit primary participant is synchronized to the existing legacy CustomerId compatibility field; changing the primary participant is transactional and never depends on list order.
A historical loading list with no participant rows remains readable through its existing CustomerId as a legacy single-customer view, without request-time writes or automatic production backfill.
Loading-list list and detail workflows expose participant count, primary Customer and a bounded participant-maintenance view without changing the identity of the container or loading list.
Adding, disabling or changing participants does not rewrite loading detail quantities, Container Booking tracking, Trade Documents, expense records, inventory or historical Customer snapshots.
Repository schema changes are idempotent and validated only through permitted local or test-database paths; production database execution remains behind the mandatory human gate.

Unit/integration tests cover multiple Customers, primary uniqueness, duplicate and inactive references, legacy single-customer compatibility, unavailable historical references and non-mutation of adjacent records; safe validation passes.
Browser/UI acceptance is recorded as deferred during development according to project policy.

scenarios: Open an existing Container Loading List, add two active Customers, designate one as primary and verify the participant count and primary Customer persist in list and detail views.

Open a legacy single-customer loading list with no participant rows, verify it remains readable without automatic writes, then attempt duplicate and inactive Customer selections and verify they are rejected.

human_gate.reason: Repository code and non-production test schema only. Production schema execution, historical backfill, deployment, release and expense posting remain behind separate human gates.
